rows.why: Most of S1 is plain summing that nobody left open. The part that was open is whether `2d` (and `1d...`) parse, which is item 2's question about which units are supported. The pick supports d, h, m, s and ms, so 2d gives 172800000. Item 6 (zero) also touches the `0s` row, but days is the closer fit.
Item 4 asks whether whitespace such as ` 1s` is accepted. S2 expects leading and trailing whitespace to be ignored, but the pick rejects all whitespace.

S3 mixes several open questions: empty string (5), bare number (1), unknown unit (2) and case (8). Most of its rows (`1.5h`, `-3s`, `+3s`, `1h 30m`, `3 s`) fall under item 4's whitespace, sign and decimal question. The pick rejects all of them, as S3 expects.
No item asks whether one component's count may exceed the size of the next unit up (`90m`). Item 3 is about unit order and repeats, and item 9 is about formatting, not parsing.
Item 3 asks whether units may come out of order or repeat. The pick requires strictly decreasing units and rejects the rest, matching S5.
Item 7 asks what the maximum duration is. The pick caps it at 2^53-1 ms, so 9007199254740991 is accepted.
Item 7 also covers what happens above the maximum. The pick returns InvalidDuration both for totals over 2^53-1 and for u64 overflow, which is what S7 expects.
Item 9 asks whether output uses the compound style or the shortest form. S8 expects greedy compound output (5400000 → `1h30m`), but the pick chooses the shortest form and prints `90m`.

This is again item 9's formatting-style question. Under the shortest-form rule, `9007199254740991ms` (18 chars) beats `104249991d8h59m991ms` (20 chars), so the pick does not give the compound string S9 expects.
No item asks whether formatting then parsing must give back the original value.
Item 11 asks what formatting does with a value above the maximum. The pick returns a MillisecondsOutOfRange error for anything above 2^53-1, which covers both rows of S11.
